script:
This is the New Saint Croix Union for Monday, November 23. Here is the week's news.

Stillwater's council met Monday night on bids for the Shoddy Mill Bergstein Warehouse Project and a task order for PFAS treatment at Well 10. The agenda also listed a second reading of a zoning text amendment for accessory structures in the Traditional Residential district, liquor and tobacco license renewals for 2027, and a temporary liquor license for the Episcopal Church of the Ascension. The meeting was at 7 p.m. The agenda did not print dollar amounts for the contracts or the task order.

Washington County commissioners met Tuesday morning for public hearings on the 2027-2031 Capital Improvement Plan and general obligation bonds under it, and on the transportation sales tax project list. They also discussed proposed 2027 property taxes, reviewed recommended budget adjustments, and considered the 2027 fee schedule. Consent items included a short-term lease at 5879 220th Street North in Forest Lake, a $1,000 donation from Hugo Yellow Ribbon Network, a $3,500 donation from Karen Marchetti for a bench at Big Marine Park Reserve, and $72,478 for library staff laptops. The meeting was at 9 a.m. in the County Board Room at the Government Center, 14949 62nd Street North, Stillwater. The agenda did not print a dollar figure for the bond issuance or a recommended levy change.

Oakdale's Environmental Management Commission met Monday night to hear a county climate action plan and review its 2027 work plan. Joe Ayers-Johnson and Macklyn Hutchison presented the Washington County Climate Action Plan in open forum. The commission discussed the draft 2027 work plan. The 2026 city-wide cleanup recycled 97 percent of materials, with more mattresses, appliances, tires, electronics, and trash than in 2025. The meeting was at 7 p.m. at the Discovery Center, 4444 Hadley Avenue North.

Oakdale's Parks and Recreation Commission met Tuesday night to review the 2027 draft work plan, which includes a 5.5 percent preliminary tax levy. Upgrades for Tanners Lake Park draw primarily from grants, including $500,000 from the Department of Natural Resources, with park preservation funds from developers. Playground maintenance upgrades cost upwards of $30,000. Pricing for the initial concept for Eberle Park has increased 20 to 30 percent from three to four years ago. The commission met at 6 p.m. at the Oakdale Discovery Center on Hadley Avenue.

Washington County conducted a recount of the Senate District 33 election on Tuesday at the Government Center in Stillwater. The recount ran from 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on Nov. 17, with Wednesday if needed, in Room 3700. The calendar did not print the prior vote margin, the number of ballots, the candidates, or who requested the recount.

The Washington County Library Board meets Monday on a construction update for the Park Grove and R.H. Stafford libraries and on dates for its 2027 meetings. The board gathers from 6:30 to 8:00 p.m. at Oakdale Library, 1010 Heron Avenue North in Oakdale. The agenda includes a consent item for the September 28 minutes, the construction update from Capital Project Manager Erik Jalowitz, 2027 meeting dates from Library Director Jacquie Kramer, statistics and updates from Kramer, and an Oakdale Library update. The agenda does not print dollar figures for the construction work.

Stillwater's Parks and Recreation Commission meets Monday night on a playground approval and next year's fee schedule. Unfinished business covers Prairie Park Playground Approval. New business includes Lumberjack Landing Reservation Policy and 2027 Fee Schedule Changes and Review. The meeting is at 6:55 p.m. The next meeting is January 25, 2027, at 7 p.m. The agenda does not print the fee amounts or the playground details.

Oakdale's council meets Tuesday on a 55-unit rental townhome project that needs a comprehensive plan amendment, a PUD change, a preliminary plat, and a site plan. Mulcahy Holdings LLC wants the homes at Cedric's Crossing. The site plan includes a $55,000 contribution toward Highway 120 improvements. Planning Commission recommended approval on October 1. Claims for November 11 through November 24 total $3,350,906.95. A Metropolitan Council Livable Communities Act grant of $1,000,000 would go to Hudson Boulevard Apartments, a 72-unit affordable project at 6700 Hudson Boulevard North, as a deferred loan with no local match. Tanners Lake TIF District No. 2-12 holds a $2.3 million surplus that would return to the county, the school district, and the city by December 31, 2027, if the district is decertified. A billboard zoning text amendment and variance in the Tanners Lake PUD is recommended for denial. The meeting is at 7 p.m. at the Discovery Center on Hadley Avenue.

Times and documents are in the show notes.
